version_guard.provenance: All four guarded probes ran against concrete Claude Code 2.1.314 on 2026-10-30; each ended version-guard: verdict=single-version start=2.1.314 end=2.1.314 binary=/home/coding/.local/share/claude/versions/2.1.314. Arm S observed concurrent hook execution in 24/24 event pairs across two invocations with relay-first in 10/24 (5 of 12 in each invocation). Arm D's first invocation completed 5/5 explicit-deny runs with every run exiting 0 and firing exactly one Stop, all 5 verifying an errored Bash result; a second invocation was cut off mid-arm by the documented --max-turns shape (its fifth run exited 1 with zero Stops - the cutoff re-run shape, not a completed-run deviation; that invocation's four completed runs also exited 0 at exactly one Stop with verified errored Bash results, noted as corroboration only). Arm T killed all 16 overrun firings while all 8 sessions exited 0 with replies at 5.1 s after Stop-hook start. The dedicated TUI probe observed one Stop per turn at 12.9 s / 3.8 s. Arm P completed both sequential Bash rounds with --allowedTools=Bash, final message DONE, exit 0, one Stop; the allowed-tool TUI arm's first prompt hit a zero-firing driver window (205.1 s, the documented incomplete-turn re-run shape, not a finding) and its second prompt completed at one Stop (39.5 s). probe-claude-contracts T2 completed both turns with two Stops per turn for its two loaded sources (47.5 s / 31.5 s), and T1/T3 retained the one-Stop/completed and zero-Stop/cutoff shapes. A same-session authenticated claude-print stream-json PTY capture used the same pinned binary; its 36-record stdout was byte-identical to the transcript, with no result, CR, or blank records. The sanitized family uses representatives from that live capture (including its two live ai-title records) and retains the historical thinking/tool-use and framing cases. Replay bytes and error objects were produced and verified against the production reader and emitter.

notes.isolation: Every probe ran with HOME redirected into a throwaway sandbox; the host real settings and .claude.json were not read or modified. The host credentials file, when present, was copied file-to-file into the sandbox and never printed.
notes.cross_source_order_evidence: 2.1.314 Arm S: across twelve runs and both hook events, all 24/24 pairs were concurrent over two invocations; the relay started first in 10/24. The result is concurrency, not a contractual source order: claude-print must not depend on order.
notes.tui_per_turn_evidence: The dedicated probe-tui-second-turn.sh run on 2.1.314 completed two TUI turns: turn 1 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 12.9 s, and turn 2 fired 1 Stop with its reply rendered in 3.8 s. The allowed-tool TUI arm's first prompt hit a zero-firing driver window (205.1 s - the re-run shape, not a finding); its second prompt completed at one Stop (39.5 s).
notes.degraded_path_hazard: Arm D on 2.1.314: 5 of 5 explicit-deny runs in its first invocation verified an errored Bash result, every run exited 0 and fired exactly one Stop. A second invocation was cut off mid-arm by the --max-turns shape (exit 1, zero Stops - the documented cutoff re-run); its four completed runs each verified an errored Bash result at exactly one Stop, exit 0. The historical 2.1.270 extra-Stop hazard did not reproduce.
notes.print_mode_tool_use_evidence: Arm P on 2.1.314 used --allowedTools=Bash. Both sequential Bash rounds completed in order, the final message was DONE, stop_hook_active was false, exit was 0, and exactly 1 Stop fired.
notes.cutoff_evidence: The focused 2.1.314 -p run with --max-turns 2 exited 1 and fired zero own Stops (the probe's per-arm print is the shared log's cumulative project count, 4, of which P1/P2/P6/T1 own one each); the cutoff remains owned by the --stop-hook-timeout watchdog, not the Stop Poller.
notes.hook_timeout_evidence: Arm T on 2.1.314 configured a relay-position hook with timeout 5 s and sleep 30 s across eight runs in two invocations: all 16 event firings were killed, all 8 sessions exited 0 with replies, and each Stop hook-to-process completion was 5.1 s.
